migrations.risk: low at apply time and medium once runtime operations begin. The migration creates one empty table and seven named indexes; it does not rewrite existing users, workspaces, resources, credentials, generations or grants. The table becomes durable recovery evidence once used: it can retain an intended folder generation, the exact grantee email and writer/reader role, an exact permission or folder receipt, retry lease and normalized failure state across a provider/database split. Four RESTRICT relationships deliberately stop a workspace, provider connection, existing storage generation or subject user from being removed while unresolved recovery work still depends on it. The target storage generation is intentionally not a foreign key because folder provision and handover must reserve that immutable id before Google returns the required folder fields for workspace_storage. Failed permission deletion remains solely in drive_folder_grants.revoke_pending beside the exact permission_id rather than being duplicated into two repair queues. A project-delete row is operational intent, not a tombstone: lifecycle code must consume it in the final workspace-delete transaction only after provider and grant cleanup. The residual risk is lifecycle code that fails to resolve or surface a manual_attention or revoke_pending row; this schema preserves that evidence rather than guessing that an ambiguous provider side effect did not happen.
migrations.rollbackPlan: Before any operation row exists: drop idx_project_drive_operations_subject_user, idx_project_drive_operations_storage, idx_project_drive_operations_connection, idx_project_drive_operations_ready, idx_project_drive_operations_workspace_status, idx_project_drive_operations_target_generation and idx_project_drive_operations_dedupe, then drop project_drive_operations. After runtime use, do not drop the journal merely to unblock a restricted delete: first stop Drive mutations, inspect every non-terminal and receipt-bearing row, reconcile the exact folder or permission at Google, complete or explicitly cancel only receipt-free intent, then remove resolved rows through a separately reviewed lifecycle operation. No rollback may delete a user's Drive file or discard a provider receipt that is still needed for repair.
postconditions: project_drive_operations exists with typed intent, provider receipt, retry, lease, bounded-error and lifecycle timestamp fields
folder provision, grant creation, rename repair, project deletion and storage handover are the only operation kinds
failed grant deletion remains in the single drive_folder_grants.revoke_pending queue with its exact permission id, not a duplicate operation kind
pending, running, retry wait, manual attention, success and safe cancellation are the only lifecycle states
dedupe keys are unique lowercase SHA-256 values and a reserved target generation can belong to only one operation
an existing storage generation is coupled to the operation workspace by a composite RESTRICT foreign key
workspace, target connection and subject-user lifecycle relationships use RESTRICT
a project-delete marker must be explicitly consumed in the final workspace-delete transaction after provider and grant cleanup
target_storage_generation_id has no premature foreign key and can be reserved before workspace_storage exists
folder and permission receipts are operation-shaped and required before their provider operations can be marked successful
grant creation retains the normalized target email and exact writer or reader role needed to recover a provider-success/database-crash split
cancelled rows cannot hide a provider receipt that requires cleanup
attempt, lease, backoff, terminal and manual-attention timestamps have consistent shapes
the table has no token, session, secret, cipher, raw-response or provider-error payload column
all tenant and recovery lookup indexes exist
the table is empty at migration time
